name: sm-01-nn-surrogate
title: NN surrogate — does it beat trivial baselines?
claim:
Tested honestly against trivial baselines under cross-validation, the neural
surrogate does NOT beat them: one-step R²≈1.0 is a persistence artifact (the
signal is smooth), and in multi-step rollout a LINEAR model is the best and
most stable emulator of coarse growth/mass while the neural net matches it at
best and destabilizes on 2/8 folds. The broad ~11.5k-observable panel is not
learnable from the observable view alone (0% of observables beat persistence).
A neural surrogate is not justified for these targets on this evidence.
question:
Does the neural-network surrogate beat trivial baselines (persistence,
mean-delta, linear) on the baseline's per-step dynamics — and are the
high-dimensional observables learnable from the observable view at all?

report.title: sm-01-nn-surrogate — surrogate fidelity vs. trivial baselines
report.evidence_quality: 8-fold leave-one-trajectory-out CV vs. baselines; per-observable skill on the broad panel
report.objective:
Honestly test whether the neural surrogate is worth its complexity: does it
beat TRIVIAL baselines (persistence = next equals current; mean-delta =
constant drift; linear = ridge regression on the per-step delta)? Measured by
cross-validated one-step fidelity AND multi-step autoregressive rollout —
the rollout being the discriminating test, since one-step is dominated by how
smooth the signal is.
report.setup:
code/rigor_eval.py runs 8-fold leave-one-trajectory-out CV over the sm-00
ensemble, training the surrogate and fitting each baseline on 7 trajectories
and evaluating on the held-out one. code/baselines.py defines the baselines.
code/rigor_eval.py --mode skill computes per-observable skill vs persistence
on the broad panel. An earlier single-split eval (compact_surrogate.html /
broad_panel_coverage.html) is retained for the per-group / parity / histogram
views; the cross-validated baseline comparison below supersedes its headline.
report.result:
COMPACT panel (mass + chromosome), 8-fold CV — one-step median per-column R²
is 1.000 for EVERY model including persistence: one-step "fidelity" is a
persistence artifact (mass-per-second is smooth), not evidence the net learned
dynamics. The discriminating multi-step rollout (cell_mass, median nRMSE):
  - linear      : 0.019   (0/8 folds unstable)   <- best, most stable
  - mean-delta  : 0.124   (0/8 unstable)
  - surrogate   : 0.032   (2/8 folds EXPLODE)    <- no better, less robust
  - persistence : 1.850   (8/8 drift badly)
BROAD panel (11569 dims), held-out: 0% of 4058 varying observables beat
persistence (negative skill everywhere); the full-vector autoregressive
rollout diverges to NaN by ~step 9.
report.interpretation:
The headline from the first pass ("near-perfect emulation, R²≈1.0") did not
survive scrutiny — it was measuring signal smoothness, not learned dynamics.
Under cross-validation against baselines:
  1. For coarse growth/mass, a LINEAR model is the best and most stable
     emulator; the neural net matches it at best and is the only model that
     destabilizes in rollout. The NN is not justified for this target.
  2. The broad high-dimensional panel is NOT learnable from the observable
     view alone (0% beat persistence) — these observables depend on the
     cell's hidden state that the panel omits. This is a property of the
     information available, not just of model capacity/data.
This is a scoping result, not a capability claim: a cheap emulator of a
smooth observable is worth building (see sm-02 utility/break-even); a neural
surrogate of the broad cell state is not supported by this evidence.
report.decision:
INFORMATIONAL — the rigorous, cross-validated finding is that the neural
surrogate does not beat trivial baselines on this target, and the high-dim
panel is unlearnable from itself. sm-03 attempts to improve on this; sm-02
quantifies the value of the cheap emulator that does work.

variants.name: compact-surrogate
variants.perturbation: Residual-MLP (64,64) on mass+chromosome (8 dims), delta parameterization.
variants.measured_contrast: mass R^2=1.000; cell_mass rollout corr 1.000; ~2700x speedup.

variants.name: broad-surrogate
variants.expected_contrast: Demonstration-grade; high-dim fidelity is the open challenge.
variants.measured_contrast: ~2% of columns R^2>0.5; rollout diverges (NaN); ~265x speedup.

tests.name: surrogate-beats-trivial-baselines
tests.question:
In cross-validated multi-step rollout, does the neural surrogate beat a
linear baseline at emulating cell_mass (ratio of surrogate to linear rollout
nRMSE < 1, i.e. lower error)?

measure.detail:
8-fold leave-one-trajectory-out CV (compact panel). Median rollout nRMSE:
surrogate 0.032 vs linear 0.019 -> ratio 1.68 (surrogate WORSE). The
surrogate also destabilizes on 2/8 folds; linear on 0/8.

tests.cites_note: Methodological: surrogate must beat the linear baseline to justify itself.

tests.name: high-dim-observables-learnable-from-panel
tests.question:
On the broad panel, does a meaningful fraction (>5%) of observables beat
persistence one-step (i.e. are they predictable from the observable view)?

measure.detail: Fraction of 4058 varying broad observables with positive skill vs persistence.

conclusion_verdicts.claim: The neural surrogate beats trivial baselines at emulating coarse growth.
conclusion_verdicts.basis: 8-fold CV: linear rollout nRMSE 0.019 (0/8 unstable) < surrogate 0.032 (2/8 explode); one-step R²=1.000 even for persistence.

conclusion_verdicts.claim: The broad high-dimensional panel is learnable from the observable view.
conclusion_verdicts.basis: 0% of 4058 varying observables beat persistence; full-vector rollout diverges to NaN.

conclusion_verdicts.claim: A cheap linear emulator is the right tool for the smooth observable, not a neural net.
conclusion_verdicts.basis: Linear is the most accurate AND most stable emulator; see sm-02 for its amortized value.

falsifiability:
The growth-emulation claim fails if the held-out cell_mass rollout correlation
drops below 0.95 or the rollout diverges. The speedup claim fails below 100x.
